releases.body:
### The ceiling is measured again, and MCP startup no longer blocks

* The agent ceiling was **stale**. Upstream's "~119" comes from an old report;
  measured on OpenCode v2.2.5 with `opencode debug agents --standalone`, **307**
  agents registered from 300 files with nothing dropped, tracking 1:1 from 110 to
  300. The default is now **300**, the refusal names the fix
  (`perun agent-catalog limit <n>`), and the Settings card keeps the message on
  screen instead of letting a toast disappear.
* `mcp/perun_mcp.py` no longer does slow work before answering the stdio
  handshake. Control-project registration and handbook indexing (which embeds
  with a 180 s request timeout) moved to a daemon thread; `init_db()` stays
  synchronous because every tool needs it and it is cheap DDL. This is the
  `mcp connect failed: Request timed out` seen in OpenCode's log after ~184 s —
  the handshake was waiting on an embedding call.

### Faster listing, and a safer bulk uninstall

* File hashes are cached by `(mtime_ns, size)`, so the Settings card no longer
  re-reads every agent file on each render; any writer invalidates the entry it
  touches. A same-size, same-timestamp rewrite is the only case it could miss.
* `remove_many` runs in **one** manifest transaction: removing a 66-agent
  division is one write instead of 66, and a failure midway keeps every earlier
  removal.
* `remove --division` supports `--dry-run` (list, change nothing) and needs
  `--yes` to actually delete; the API takes `dry_run` too.
* The Installed list gains a division filter, and an `unlisted` agent (adopted,
  hash still matching) now offers **Remove** instead of only **Forget**.

### Uninstall stays inside the scope you named

* `remove --division <name> --project <slug>` (and the equivalent API call) now
  removes only that project's copies. It previously matched every agent of the
  division, including the machine-wide ones, because the scope was not part of
  the filter.
* `POST /api/agent-catalog/remove` with an empty `paths` list is a clear 400
  (*"choose agents (paths) or a division"*) instead of falling through to a
  single-file removal of the empty path.

### Uninstall from the dashboard, and Perun's own agents are untouchable

* Settings → **Agent roster** → **Installed** lists every installed agent with a
  **Remove** button, a per-division removal chip (*Remove engineering (66)*), and
  **Forget** for an edited one — an edited file is never deleted. Removal keeps a
  backup, and OpenCode picks up installs and removals on its next start.
* `GET /api/agent-catalog/installed` returns compact rows (no descriptions) and
  `POST /api/agent-catalog/remove` accepts `path`, `paths` or `division`. CLI:
  `perun agent-catalog installed`, `perun agent-catalog remove --division <name>`.
* **Perun's own agents are explicitly protected.** `perun-*` templates and the
  chat persona can no longer be adopted, installed over, promoted or deleted by
  the catalogue, and are never listed. Before, that held only because they are
  not in the roster index — an accident, not a rule.
* The roster stays opt-in: nothing is installed by default, and every install is
  removable from the same card.
* The runtime baseline is only applied when the runtime reports at least one of
  Perun's roster files; if it is looking at another directory the two counts
  describe different machines, and the guard falls back to counting files
  (`slots.baseline_source` says which).

### The agent ceiling is a setting, not a magic number

* `perun agent-catalog limit <n>` — or the **Agent ceiling** field on the
  Settings card — sets the ceiling for this machine. It is stored in the roster
  manifest, defaults to the upstream-reported 119, and is bounded to 1–1000. This
  runtime registers **120** with nothing dropped, so an operator who re-measures
  their build can raise it without waiting for a Perun release.
* `slots()` uses the configured value for `limit`, `remaining` and the install
  guard, and the CLI reports when the machine is at the ceiling.
* `tests/test_agents.py` now isolates the global agent directory instead of
  reading the operator's real 113-agent install, and the install path gained a
  positive project-scope test.

### The roster guard counts registered agents, not files

* `install` adds the runtime's non-roster baseline — built-ins, Perun's own
  agents, anything hand-written — to the file count before comparing with the
  ~119 ceiling. Counting files alone understated the budget by exactly that
  baseline, so the last handful of agents could still be dropped. `status`
  reports `baseline` and `projected`, and the CLI says when the machine is at the
  ceiling.
* An upgrade backs up the file it replaces, and `promote` backs up before
  rewriting it — the same rule `remove` already followed.
* Manifest mutations (adopt/accept/forget/remove/promote/install) now hold the
  lock across read-modify-write, so two concurrent changes cannot drop an entry.
* A project-scoped install skips a slug that already exists globally instead of
  writing a shadowed copy that Perun's discovery would never list.
* `available?project=<slug>` marks project-local installs; `status?agents=false`
  omits the per-agent list (the panels only need the counts).
* `tools/agency_index.py` refuses to write an index when it cannot resolve
  `main`, instead of quietly recording `main` and following the branch.

### Roster audit fixes

* An index `slug` is validated (`[a-z0-9-]`) before it can become a filename, so
  a hand-edited or corrupt index can never write outside the agents directory.
* An install saves the manifest even when one file fails mid-run: a locked file
  or a full disk can no longer leave untracked agents on disk that Perun would
  then refuse to touch. A failed write is reported as a skip, and its temp file
  is removed.
* Oversized archive members are skipped. The compressed download was capped; the
  decompressed member was not.
* The project roster panel no longer claims Perun never installs — it has since
  v0.16.1. The static test now asserts the copy instead of the stale claim.

### Install the roster from Settings

Perun can now install Agency Agents itself, from the Settings page — no bash, no
separate app, no terminal.

* Settings → **Agent roster**: pick divisions (each with its agent count) and
  install into the global agents directory. The slot meter shows what the runtime
  actually registered (`opencode debug agents`), not what is on disk.
* The install is **pinned**: it downloads the snapshot at the commit recorded in
  `perun/data/agency_index.json` and converts it with upstream's rules (quoted
  scalars, the named-colour table, body verbatim). Nothing follows upstream's
  branch between Perun releases, and the tarball is cached so a re-install works
  offline.
* It refuses to exceed the ~119-agent ceiling, refuses to overwrite an agent
  Perun does not track, and refuses to overwrite one whose hash changed since it
  was installed. Upstream's own installer still works: `adopt` takes over its
  output.
* `GET /api/agent-catalog/available` lists the roster with an `installed` flag;
  `POST /api/agent-catalog/install` takes `divisions`, `agents`, `scope`
  (`global`/`project`) and `limit`. CLI: `perun agent-catalog available|install`.
* Project-scoped installs are supported by the API and the CLI
  (`install … --project <slug>`).

### Third-party agent rosters: custody, not acquisition

Perun can now track an external OpenCode agent roster — the Agency Agents set —
without installing or converting it. Upstream's installer (or its desktop app)
stays the only thing that writes agent files; Perun records provenance, counts
the runtime's real registration budget, protects edited copies and removes
cleanly.

* `perun/agent_catalog.py` + `perun/data/agency_index.json`: a build-time index
  (`tools/agency_index.py`, pinned commit, 268 agents / 18 divisions) so
  recognition is offline and never parses upstream markdown at runtime.
* Custody states: `candidate`, `adopted`, `modified`, `unlisted`; hashes and
  `mode_intent` live in `PERUN_HOME/agent_catalog.json`.
* `opencode debug agents` is the source of truth for what registered — files on
  disk cannot show the silent drop past ~119. `slots()` reports `registered`,
  `remaining` and the files that did not register.
* Guard rails: `remove` refuses an edited agent and backs up first; `preflight`
  names what a re-install would overwrite (the upstream installer copies over an
  existing file with no backup); `promote` makes a `subagent` selectable as a Run
  agent and re-baselines its hash; `team` refuses a selection over the ceiling.
* API `GET /api/agent-catalog/{status,preflight,team}` and
  `POST /api/agent-catalog/{adopt,accept,forget,remove,promote,backup}`; CLI
  `perun agent-catalog …`; a compact "Agent roster" panel in the project config
  card. No MCP tools: this mutates the operator's agent directory.
* `GET /api/agents?project=<slug>` scans the project's `.opencode/agents/`, so
  project-local agents (where upstream installs by default) finally appear in
  Perun's pickers; the machine-wide call is unchanged and the cache is keyed by
  project.

### VS Code: per-project client count for Mode B

* `GET /api/vscode/status?project=<slug>` returns `project_clients`; the
  dashboard only attempts a VS Code terminal when **this** project has a
  connected companion, so a window open for another project no longer causes a
  failed request and a fallback notice.
* The decision is a pure module (`web/js/vscode_launch.js`) covered by
  `extensions/vscode/tests/vscode_launch.test.js`: untrusted or no client →
  external terminal with the matching notice; a trusted connected window
  overrides a stale untrusted heartbeat.
